notes: Company: mid-market SaaS (B2B search + analytics). Product teams evaluating semantic search to improve relevance across docs and support articles.
Primary goal: improve search relevance + reduce time-to-first-answer for support agents. Target: 50-150ms retrieval latency for top-K, and sustain nightly batch embed jobs of ~500k docs.
Current stack: Postgres + S3 for raw docs; evaluating Pinecone vs Weaviate for vector store; prefer a managed vector DB but open to self-hosted if cost-effective.
POC ask: Hosted API for fast evaluation (embeddings endpoint + example reranking flow), then Dedicated for predictable throughput and lower unit cost if POC meets SLA.
Throughput requirements: need to embed up to 2M docs/month (batching overnight), plus near-real-time ingestion for user-created docs (~200/day).

Observed during demo: Hosted API embedding throughput for small batch test was ~1.2k embeddings/min with batch=256; SE notes this will need Dedicated to meet sustained nightly throughput with predictable cost.

Latency sensitivity: search path includes embedding lookup + vector DB kNN + optional reranking. Want <200ms p95 for search queries in most regions. Cost sensitivity moderate — will trade some cost for reliability but wants clear unit economics.
Security: must meet SSO (SAML), audit logs, KMS integration for keys, and EU data residency for EU customers. Legal requested Redwood security FAQ + SOC2 evidence.
Quote from Head of Product: "If we can get consistent nightly batch performance and a reasonable price for Dedicated, we can move aggressively."
Quote from CTO: "Main risk is vector DB integration and peak throughput — need to validate end-to-end."
